facts.text: 開発者を一人も知らなかったため、友人の友人（Grant Mac）に案を話し、すぐに協力を得た。
2014 年に Product Hunt で Poolside FM として公開し、Reddit の r/InternetIsBeautiful にも投稿した。記事によると、Reddit で「少し」話題になり、公開は Vice と Manrepeller に取り上げられた。
2021 年 6 月の取材では、Poolsuite に取り組むチームは 10 人と紹介された。
2021 年 6 月 10 日の記事は、Vacation by Poolsuite の正式発売が当日で、Product Hunt の先行公開は 4 月だったと記載した。Vacation by Poolsuite は同社の新しい日焼け止めで、最初の物理的な製品である。
本人は Jacuzzi Club の Slack で相談し、日焼け止めの処方を開発していた Lach と Dakota から連絡を受け、後に Vacation の共同創業者に加わったと説明した。
Vacation の Classic Lotion SPF 50 は、2023 年の登場以来、2025 年 9 月の取材までに約 150 万本販売したと本人が述べた。これは Vacation の商品販売数であり、Poolsuite の売上ではない。
2025 年 9 月の本人回答では、Poolsuite は iOS と Android の新しい音楽アプリを公開し、直前の週末に Los Angeles でパーティーを開いた。
App Store の掲載では、販売者は POOLSIDE WORLDWIDE CORPORATION LTD で、Poolsuite FM は無料と表示されている。
2020 年 10 月 1 日の Trevor Peach のレビューは、最初は見た目で入れたが使ってから気に入り、友人にも勧め、ほかの音楽アプリの多くを使わなくなったと述べた。
2021 年 10 月 12 日の Mikezila のレビューは、見た目と機能を評価する一方、SoundCloud の上限表示で音が出ないことが多く、代わりにウェブ版を使っていると述べた。これは 1 人の当時の経験である。
App Store の版 2.0.0 の変更説明は、常時流れる新しい音楽配信を備え、安定性を高めた macOS 版を公開したと記載している。表示には 4 月 21 日のみで年がないため、年は採用しない。

What Marty Bell, founder of Poolsuite, has to say about building for fun
Poolsuite doesn’t track KPIs. Bell doesn’t call himself a CEO. He and the ragtag group of designers & developers who work on the “virtual vacation” station just have fun.
Sarah Wright June 10th, 2021
About Poolsuite Poolsuite is the ultimate summer music player.
Grab another Banana Daiquiri and pick from a number of sun-drenched music channels, each lovingly curated with the sole purpose of lifting your spirits.
Available on web, iOS and Android
Marty Bell may be from the (stunning yet) cold Scottish Highlands, but that hasn’t stopped him from being the unofficial keeper of summer.
Bell is the founder of Poolsuite (formerly Poolside FM ), the radio station, website, and brand that epitomizes summer nostalgia with retro 80s graphics and vibey relaxing music. As a recent Maker Grant recipient and off today's official launch of Vacation by Poolsuite (which pre-launched on Product Hunt in April), I spoke with Bell about his maker story.
We started by talking about how the dreary weather may have been part of why he started working on Poolsuite.
“Everyone thinks we’re from LA... I was probably subconsciously trying to getaway from the grey of Scotland when the idea arose,” he explained.
Poolsuite just became a finalist for the 2021 Apple Design Awards and made news for its partnership with Playdate . It’s also a favorite in the Product Hunt community too (we sometimes kick off our all-hands meetings here with the station while we wait for everyone to join the Zoom). Take a look at a few of the latest Poolsuite comments.
The vibes are unreal!!! 🤙🌴🍹Thank you for this!!!! ! Jan Köster
It's a modern time capsule of sexy. Chad Fullerton
I am not leaving this app anytime soon. Aakarshna Anand
As a native Angeleno living in London, I can’t help but feel nostalgic myself when I’m on Poolsuite, but I love that you don’t have to live anywhere or be born at any one time to appreciate it. The aesthetics and jams are inclusive in a way that people all over the world can enjoy a bit of ultra summer.
How it started
Today, community is the foundation many makers build their products upon. Experts often tout the importance of having peers so you can support each other’s projects and find early adopters. As it happened, Bell didn’t have any following or community before he started Poolsuite.
“When I first launched it I wasn’t building digital products, I was building brands and making physical products. Then I stumbled upon this super-happy genre-spanning kind of music and I loved it so much; it felt like (and still does feel like) a direct hit of serotonin straight to the brain to me.. I thought ‘I could build a playlist and share it with people. But everyone shares playlists that barely anyone listens to. I need to build an experience around it to make it spread.’”
Bell wanted to pair the music with something else that would make it even more powerful. Even though the music was new, it reminded him of 80s summer beach movies, the kind you instinctively picture coming on a VHS tape (if you’re old enough to have used one regularly).
The idea to create an 80s style website dawned on Bell.
“When I think of the 80s in the U.S. I always picture some kind of LA beach scene in my head, bursting with carefree good times and positivity. No iPhones, no WiFi, no plans.”
The only problem was...
“I didn’t even know a single developer at the time. I didn’t know what web apps were outside of the terrible things I was installing on some very questionable WordPress site builds around that time. But I reached out to a friend of a friend (shoutout Grant Mac!) and pitched him the idea, he said he was in immediately."
The friend was thrilled to help — it sounded like fun. Bell got to work pulling creative assets to “throw together” a website. What the movies were didn’t even matter. He hadn’t seen half of them. What was important was pairing the scenes with music so that he could re-create the feeling he got while listening.
That’s part of the brilliance of Poolsuite. The site isn’t so closely tied to one source of inspiration or reference to pop culture. It truly is a vibe.
How it's going
Bell launched Poolside FM on Product Hunt in 2014, i.e. not long after Product Hunt was born. It's since undergone a re-name to Poolsuite (Bell and team explained the change here ).
Since it was seven years ago, Bell had to go back through his profile history to try to remember what happened at the beginning. Though the comments on the post are few, they are as welcoming and energetic as the Poolsuite app that launched last week.
I'm in love. Totally rad! Big 80s fan so loving the vibe. Will be great on TV for summer time parties. :) - Corey Gwin
Bookmarked this immediately <3 - Lejla Bajgoric
Awesome find! Really love the 80s feel! - Adrian Grant
Beyond Product Hunt, Bell posted Poolsuite to the subreddit r/InternetIsBeautiful/, where it went “a bit viral” and the launch was covered by Vice and Manrepeller.
“From then, I’ve never tried to turn it into a business. This has been a fun thing on the side — a digital playground. Our incredibly talented gang of designers & developers jam on it and we see how fast we can push things out in evenings and weekends. Most of my job is to curate the content and make sure the contriburing team are having a great time.”
Bell curates and art directs Poolsuite and its products, including Vacation by Poolsuite , the company’s new sunscreen, and first physical product. He stressed though that he’s “definitely not a designer,” a job that’s handled by Neik Dekker, one of a team of 10 people currently working on the Poolsuite. Still, he works side-by-side with Neik, obsessing over the design research and “over-doing things” authentically.
We touched on how the old school operating system design that you see when you launch Poolsuite is core to the experience (and how Poparazzi’s onboarding flow recently exploded in a similar vein).
“I love any products that make you think 'Wait, what the hell is this thing?!' Things that take people a few seconds to work out. We like to see the Poolsuite website and apps like mini sensory experiences, or virtual toys."
Expansion doesn’t have to be a buzzkill
Most of what Poolsuite puts out is still free and Bell keeps it that way.
“My job is to make it fun. We don’t try to track KPIs or metrics. I think that comes out in the product. I’ve seen a few tweets that said something along the lines of 'I can tell how much fun this team is having just by using the app/site,' and that’s absolutely true. We’re optimizing for fun, and excitement —even just our own. Nothing else. I think the whole project would’ve died a long time ago if I took it too seriously or tried to directly monetize it.”
That’s not to say he’s always had a clear picture of what to do with the product and community he’s built. He reached out to his Slack community, Jacuzzi Club, a couple of years ago for help deciding what to do next with Poolsuite while he was too busy with another startup to focus his energy on it.
That’s how he met Lach Hall & Dakota Green, a match made in poolside heaven. Hall & Green had the concept and formulation for a new sunscreen but no brand. They were just about to raise money for the new company when Bell entered the chat looking for new opportunities, both of the fun and business nature. That’s how Vacation was born.
“Sunscreen is the perfect product. We’d been offered dozens of opportunities and collabs over the years — craft beer, swimwear brands, pool floats. Everything obvious wasn’t exciting to me. We like to go all-in on stuff and go deep on brand and personality. Sunscreen is one of the few products you can layer deep nostalgia into.”
And they went all-in on “The World’s Best Smelling Sunscreen.” The product was crafted to transport you to the summer of 1986, Miami, Florida, and not just via the smell — which incorporates scents of coconut and banana — but through the whole experience, from the way the packaging opens to the receipt printed on old school 80s printer paper.
Building for fun
This is one of the key reasons Poolsuite has kept its cool factor and edge over the last seven years (and growing) — Bell’s insistency on keeping it a side project. He has never been focused on growth metrics and really is just having fun.
“In building projects, so many people are so obsessed with being a founder. Especially when you’re younger. But whatever you can do to make your projects more relaxed you should do. There’s no advantage to being overly serious … except maybe in something like medicine.”
Bell tells aspiring makers that the way they position something they’re working on matters. He calls what he’s working on “experiments” and that leaves him open to working with friends. He doesn’t position himself as a CEO and would caution others on doing so quickly too. When you’re a CEO, you have to do everything right.
“There’s been no pressure on me to deliver whatsoever. If you’re having fun with everything, and keep your project lighthearted, when there’s a bug or critical failure, you can laugh it off.”
This attitude has allowed Bell to pull in talented developers to work on Poolsuite in return for a stress-free space to get creative, hone their skills, and have a good time.
“A product is a vehicle to have a fun exciting life and no one thinks about it that way. You can build a brand or project and, even if it just covers costs but you get an opportunity to meet interesting people and learn how building stuff works, it’s more than worthwhile.
There should be a course on how to build a really fun side project. Not to make money, just to make your life more exciting.”
Who else would take that class?

Q&A: Poolsuite and Vacation®'s Marty Bell
"A poolside daiquiri, a 1983 hotel TV commercial, a beach bag full of coconut-banana-scented memories."
Hannah Bronfman
Sep 05, 2025
4
Share
This Hannah’s List series highlights the founders (and strategies) behind the brands we love. In this edition: Marty Bell, co-founder of Poolsuite and Vacation®.
Have you ever come across that quote — and I’m definitely paraphrasing it here — but it goes something like: I’m nostalgic for summer but for summer 1993. I think about that all the time. There’s something about the way certain seasons, certain years, stick with you. And scent plays such a big role in that. It’s like an instant time machine. And for so many of us, the smell of sunscreen immediately brings us back to a carefree childhood summers. Everyone is nostalgic for the smell of SPF.
The contents of my Cabo beach bag. The Vacation® Classic Lotion has the brand’s signature scent: notes of coconut, banana (and pool water, pool toy and swimsuit). The formula is dreamy. Rubs in fast and uses coconut oil, aloe vera, banana extract, vitamin d, and niacinamide.
Subscribe
Now that technology is at our fingertips, most of us are much more mindful about the products we use. Efficacy has become the #1 priority which is (mostly) great. The flip side of that is a lot of products end up feeling really clinical which can come across as intimidating or, honestly, boring. That’s what makes Vacation® different. The packaging is fun and clever, think the original Baywatch in a bottle, but the real reason people keep coming back — it actually works.
I don’t think I’ve packed a single beach bag without at least one Vacation® product since the brand launched. My regulars are the Super Spritz SPF 50 (easy to reapply) and the Classic Lotion (no white cast).
I got to chat with Marty Bell about the brand and the digital mixtapes (yes, really) that lead to the creation of this kitschy and cool SPF universe.
A snapshot of the Vacation® product ~suite~
"A poolside daiquiri, a 1983 hotel TV commercial, a beach bag full of coconut-banana-scented memories."
Tell us a bit about your early career. Where did you start, and what were your initial aspirations?
I attempted university for a year in Edinburgh, Scotland but dropped out after falling head over heels in love with the idea of the lifestyle brand. I realised you could wrap a bunch of your interests in a thing called a brand, then try to make a business out of it. My first business at the age of 18 was a small-time nightlife-focused internet clothing brand selling basic merch and throwing parties with some of our favourite DJs. I did that for ~4 very chaotic years before realising I was ready to try something a bit more serious. I then started an internet sunglasses brand, and around the same time, a little music website called Poolside FM which would end up dramatically changing the trajectory of my life.
The Poolsuite mix tapes are genuinely so good. Hannah-the-DJ-approved.
What was the moment you knew you wanted to start a sunscreen brand? And how did it go from idea to reality?
Seven years into running that music website, which had by then renamed to ‘Poolsuite’, it suddenly hit a major organic viral streak with over a million people tuning-in a year. I was caught up in a fintech startup I co-founded, with little time to know what to do with all the hype and attention it was receiving. I posted in a Slack channel for founders I’d put together - Jacuzzi Club - asking for advice, and shortly after received a DM from a strange Australian and American duo named Lach & Dakota who told me they’d been developing ‘leisure-enhancing’ sunscreen formulas and wondered if there may be a way to build out a sunscreen company as an extension of the eccentric Poolsuite brand world. I instantly fell in love with the idea and flew to meet them in NYC a few weeks later. Shortly after, I joined as a co-founder of Vacation®.
The Vacation® website is super interactive with all these nods to nostalgia. This little coupon section at the bottom of the site is my favorite.
Give us a bit of a company overview, from concept to cult-gether.
Vacation was born out of an obsession with bringing back the joy we saw in sunscreen brands of the ‘80s, before everything went (rightfully) ultra-clinical and serious. In the depths of Covid, we decided to immerse ourselves in the leisure lifestyle and hunkered down together in a tiny tropical beach town in the Dominican Republic for what was meant to be a month-long creative retreat, which somehow turned into almost a year. I had a golf cart as my daily driver, and Lach & I engaged in deeply humiliating personal training sessions 3 times a week in front of the local beach bar, trying to work off the banana daiquiris which were powering the product, brand & launch strategy that was slowly but surely coming together.
On whiteboards set up by the pool, we mapped out the concept for the honorary job roles we’d give out to anyone who wanted to be a part of the brand, like Breakfast Buffet Specialist and Hot Tub Temperature Analyst; which ~10,000 people ended up claiming pre-launch. But beneath all the silliness in the brand was also true innovation and science - a luxurious SPF formula developed with Dr. Elizabeth Hale, leading dermatologist, packaging designed to make you smile, and an iconic scent developed by Carlos Huber of ARQUISTE Parfumeur and Rodrigo Flores-Roux of Givaudan.
Vacation is all about making SPF fun. What did “fun” mean to you when you first launched, and how has that evolved?
We wanted to flip the script and bring joy back to the sunscreen aisle. To us, fun meant reveling in that universally shared, quintessential “vacation” mindset. A poolside daiquiri, a 1983 hotel TV commercial, a beach bag full of coconut-banana-scented memories. People want to feel good about taking care of themselves. If our whipped-cream sunscreen makes you smile, you’ll probably reach for it more often . That’s real impact.
Sunscreen can feel clinical and boring. What was the biggest challenge in flipping that perception?
The challenge was getting people to believe we could be fun while still being serious about sun protection. When you’re launching sunscreen in a whipped cream can, people assume it’s all novelty. But we worked with Dr. Elizabeth Hale, a leading dermatologist and SVP of the Skin Cancer Foundation, and top-tier FDA-certified labs to make formulas that really work. It had to be fun, effective, and safe at the end of it all. Once people tried it, they got it.
You’ve had some pretty iconic product drops. Which launch felt like, OK we’re doing something special here?
For me, it was our very first product - The Classic Lotion SPF 30. It launched with no legacy, no track record, just a wild brand idea and a commitment to making sunscreen fun again. But people got it instantly. The retro-style packaging, the nostalgic scent, the tone of voice - it all clicked. It was then that it became clear we weren’t just launching a product, we were building a brand world that people wanted to be a part of.
What has been your biggest failure? Your biggest success?
Biggest failure is maybe not launching Vacation® in 2017… or not hiring a Head of Sales earlier… or our continued failure to convince the board we must acquire a corporate seaplane for “business” throughout the Florida Keys. In terms of success, we’ve had nearly 1.5 million tubes of our Classic Lotion SPF 50 sold to date since its original inception back in 2023, and I’d also say another huge success is the organic viral traction we’ve received on TikTok with Classic Whip receiving hundreds of millions of views. We designed these products with a whole lot of love and attention to detail, so to witness a community who loves them and genuinely wants to talk about them is incredible to see.
What’s a piece of advice you’d go back and tell yourself when you first launched?
When I first launched Poolsuite, I wish I’d given myself more time and space to explore ideas just for the sake of it, without any kind of business model or strategy.
“Looking back, the projects I started purely to make money have almost never worked. Poolsuite was just a web music player with looping ‘80s beach scenes, and Vacation® began with a ridiculous 42-page pitch novella. My best work always seems to start with a weird idea that I can’t stop thinking about.”
We love a teaser. Can you give us a hint at what’s coming next? Even just a vibe?
On the Vacation® side, expect more leisure-enhancing formats, some surprising collaborations, and some pretty wild campaigns next year. Same mission: make sunscreen fun. At Poolsuite we’re building out our suite of ultra-summer apps (we just released our beautiful new music app on iOS and Android) and we’re putting together a bunch more parties like the one we just hosted in LA over the weekend, with some of the hottest DJs around.
Anyone you want to see in the next Q&A? Drop their names in the comments.

SOMA FM's 16-bit baby sister?
08/19/2021 Tofu Musubi
Poolsuite FM app feels like SOMA FM's 16-bit baby sister. Poolsuite FM similarly streams music in a selection of channels. There are currently six channels: Poolsuite FM; Latest 20 Tracks; Indie Summer; Hangover Club; Tokyo Disco; and Friday Nite Heat. There's little difference between these; all channels play synth-driven, dreamy vocal tracks with a late 80s / early 90s vibe. If you're looking for light, vaguely pleasant but ultimately forgettable music to stream in a coffeeshop background inoffensively, Poolsuite FM may be the app for you.

1.2.1 10/16/2021
WE HAVE A NEW NAME... Introducing "Poolsuite"
Dear Beloved Patrons of the Pool,
You have been with us through doubt and through certitude. Through thick and thin. And once again, we ask for your unwavering support.
Unbeknownst to many, Poolside FM has undergone an ocean liner sized challenge with the law regarding intellectual property rights surrounding "Poolside FM" as our associated brand name. What would begin as a trademark infringement lawsuit would soon develop into a saga of contention, malfeasance, and deceit.
Troubled Times
For almost 4 years we have evaded the hard hand of the law through a multitude of high-stakes relocations throughout the Caribbean basin. Grasping dearly to the household name you all know and love. Out of desperation we made a questionable arrangement with the St Lucian Mafioso to protect us from the USPTO and various international rights holders. Inevitably, this only deepened our Mariana Trench of problems. Spending days in reckless speedboat chases and sleepless nights on uncharted islands, with nothing but cocktail napkins for blankets. It was only a few years ago that mounting a D-30 turbofan jet engine to a 1986 Wellcraft 38 Scarab KV would be a misuse of the company budget. But a few wrong moves with the Caribbean Cartel would prove this procedure to be an extortionate yet core component to our survival.
Moving Forward
We have gone to the ends of the earth – literally – to avoid drastic measures, with generous plea bargains put forth by our team of nautical attorneys. But ultimately not even collections of valuable tropical fish, light aircrafts filled with Lambrusco wine and fine Italian meats, or a specially built sea-faring Ferrari 308 GTS would be enough to feed the USPTO’s insatiable hunger for injustice. The only way out was to wave a white sail. Not as a surrender to the law. But as a token to mark the monumental restructuring of our corporate identity.
Today we resign our troubled past overseas. Today we make a new name for ourselves. Today we return home as…
Poolsuite™
Luxurious yet leisurely. Frivolous yet sophisticated. The same sweet sound of summer— turned up to 11. Pack your virtual bags as you've been upgraded from sitting poolside to a private cabana at The Poolsuite. Lie back as we embark on an ambitious worldwide expansion, bringing you a rich suite of virtual tools & leisure products to give you delicately towards "The Good Life" from the comfort of your daybed.
Thank you for your unshakeable commitment to our cherished enterprise.
And as always, we'll see you by the pool.

analysis.text: App Store では Poolsuite FM は無料と表示されている。販売者は POOLSIDE WORLDWIDE CORPORATION LTD。
2014年に Product Hunt で Poolside FM として公開し、同時に Reddit の r/InternetIsBeautiful へ投稿した。Reddit で少し話題になり、公開は Vice と Manrepeller に取り上げられた。
口コミで広がっている可能性がある。2020年10月1日の App Store レビューで、ある利用者は、見た目に惹かれて入れたアプリを使ううちに気に入ったと書いた。友人にも勧め、ほかの音楽アプリの多くを使わなくなったという。2025年9月の取材で Bell は、直前の週末に Los Angeles でパーティーを開いたと述べており、画面の外でも接点を作っている。
始めた時点で本人は開発者を一人も知らず、友人の友人の Grant Mac に案を話して協力を得た。2021年6月の取材時点では、Poolsuite に取り組むチームは10人だった。
アプリは App Store で配っている。2021年10月の利用者レビューでは、SoundCloud の上限表示が出て音が鳴らないことが多く、代わりにウェブ版を使っていると書かれている。1人の当時の経験だが、音源の配信が外部サービスの上限に左右される場面があったことを示している。
弱いと見られる。音楽アプリは無料で、1件のレビューでは、アプリで音が出ない時にウェブ版へ移って聞いていたと書かれている。客をつなぎ止めているのは、主に見た目と世界観への好みだと推す。

2014年：Product Hunt で Poolside FM として公開し、Reddit にも投稿。2021年4月：Vacation by Poolsuite を Product Hunt で先行公開。2021年6月10日：Vacation by Poolsuite を正式発売。2023年：Classic Lotion SPF 50 が登場。2025年9月：iOS と Android の新しい音楽アプリを公開し、Los Angeles でパーティーを開催。
開発者を一人も知らないまま友人の友人に案を持ち込み、2014年に Product Hunt と Reddit へ出した無料の音楽サイトを、日焼け止めブランド Vacation の立ち上げにつなげた。
無料の音楽サイトで育てた世界観を、Slack の仲間経由で出会った処方開発者の日焼け止めに載せ、物販に移した。本人の発言では、売った物は約150万本にのぼる。

facts.text: 開発者を一人も知らなかったため、友人の友人（Grant Mac）に案を話し、すぐに協力を得た。
2014 年に Product Hunt で Poolside FM として公開し、Reddit の r/InternetIsBeautiful にも投稿した。記事によると、Reddit で「少し」話題になり、公開は Vice と Manrepeller に取り上げられた。
2021 年 6 月の取材では、Poolsuite に取り組むチームは 10 人と紹介された。
2021 年 6 月 10 日の記事は、Vacation by Poolsuite の正式発売が当日で、Product Hunt の先行公開は 4 月だったと記載した。Vacation by Poolsuite は同社の新しい日焼け止めで、最初の物理的な製品である。
本人は Jacuzzi Club の Slack で相談し、日焼け止めの処方を開発していた Lach と Dakota から連絡を受け、後に Vacation の共同創業者に加わったと説明した。
Vacation の Classic Lotion SPF 50 は、2023 年の登場以来、2025 年 9 月の取材までに約 150 万本販売したと本人が述べた。これは Vacation の商品販売数であり、Poolsuite の売上ではない。
2025 年 9 月の本人回答では、Poolsuite は iOS と Android の新しい音楽アプリを公開し、直前の週末に Los Angeles でパーティーを開いた。
App Store の掲載では、販売者は POOLSIDE WORLDWIDE CORPORATION LTD で、Poolsuite FM は無料と表示されている。
2020 年 10 月 1 日の Trevor Peach のレビューは、最初は見た目で入れたが使ってから気に入り、友人にも勧め、ほかの音楽アプリの多くを使わなくなったと述べた。
2021 年 10 月 12 日の Mikezila のレビューは、見た目と機能を評価する一方、SoundCloud の上限表示で音が出ないことが多く、代わりにウェブ版を使っていると述べた。これは 1 人の当時の経験である。
App Store の版 2.0.0 の変更説明は、常時流れる新しい音楽配信を備え、安定性を高めた macOS 版を公開したと記載している。表示には 4 月 21 日のみで年がないため、年は採用しない。

開発者を一人も知らないまま友人の友人に案を持ち込み、2014年に Product Hunt と Reddit へ出した無料の音楽サイトを、日焼け止めブランド Vacation の立ち上げにつなげた。
無料の音楽サイトで育てた世界観を、Slack の仲間経由で出会った処方開発者の日焼け止めに載せ、物販に移した。本人の発言では、売った物は約150万本にのぼる。
